articles.title: PLANETS FOR POETS
articles.summary: Foothill College is offering "Planets for Poets," an introductory Astronomy 10A course for the winter quarter of January through March 2006. Taught by Andrew Fraknoi, the course requires no prior science or math background and covers a range of engaging topics from new planetary discoveries to cosmic threats and the search for extraterrestrial life. Registration begins December 12th for both day and evening sessions.

articles.title: Dobson Workshop at Jan/Feb Astronomy Class
articles.summary: Rob Hawley will lead a two-part workshop in January and February, focusing on Dobsonian/Newtonian telescopes. The first session on January 20 will cover setup issues, collimation techniques, tools, hands-on practice, and scope maintenance, including cleaning optics and dealing with dew. The second session on February 17 will focus on using the scope, discussing filters, star charts (paper and PC), planning observing sessions, object catalogs, finding objects, and keeping records.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides an astronomical guide for January, detailing optimal observing conditions for planets such as Mars and Saturn, the latter reaching opposition with a noticeable ring tilt. It also covers the return of the Stardust spacecraft carrying comet dust, and celestial events like the gibbous moon passing through the Pleiades. Furthermore, it explains Earth's perihelion occurring in winter and clarifies that seasons are caused by axial tilt, not distance from the sun.

articles.title: Observe the Stardust Re-entry
articles.summary: The Stardust spacecraft is scheduled for re-entry on January 15, 2006, at 1:56 PST, returning pristine samples of comet Wild 2 and interstellar dust to land in Utah. This event will be the fastest spacecraft re-entry ever, creating a visible 'scheduled meteor' across the western United States, with a predicted peak magnitude of -7. NASA will be studying the re-entry from a DC-8, and amateur astronomers are encouraged to observe and submit photographic or video data, with specific viewing guidance provided for locations in Nevada and Utah.

articles.title: Michael Detweiler, 1942 - 2005
articles.summary: Michael Burnside Detweiler, a distinguished chemist and physicist, passed away on December 3, 2005, at the age of 63, after a long battle with prostate cancer. Throughout his career, he made significant contributions, including developing an improved hemoccult test for early colon cancer and working on rocket propellants, while also passionately tutoring students in science. A lifelong astronomy enthusiast and member of the San Jose Astronomical Association, he also found joy as a skilled pianist.

articles.title: A New View of the Andromeda Galaxy
articles.summary: The article discusses a new perspective on the Andromeda Galaxy, revealed by NASA's GALEX ultraviolet telescope. While typically seen as a spiral, GALEX's UV imaging, which highlights newborn stars, shows Andromeda as a vast ring of star formation around a concentrated core. This new view helps astronomers understand galaxy evolution by studying star birth patterns in Andromeda and numerous other galaxies, both nearby and billions of light-years away.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, detailing which telescopes are available for immediate loan to members and providing contact information for borrowing. It also lists scopes that are currently loaned out or on extended loan, including their borrowers and due dates. The program offers a wide variety of telescopes, from small refractors to large Dobsons, as a benefit for SJAA members.
